title: New white and Black bands appear; Local 802 contract rules
summary: Dorsey, Goodman, Lombardo and others start up; Local 802 forbade working with two bands.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: And then, here the band started jumping up, too. The Dorsey Brothers and (inaudible) Benny Goodman, Guy Lombardo, he started in '28, Guy. Vincent Lopez, he started, too. And slowly but surely, each year a different band would show up. Well, they were colored bands that came to New York, too. And, of course, when they got here, I was here.

Well, you couldn't work with no more than one band at a time, because we belonged to Local 802. If you sign up for one band, you got to play with that band. You can't break your contract. But I could have played with a different band. But when I'm with one, I had to stay with one.
